title: EU Sovereignty Routing Enforcer: customer allowlist/denylist + residency tags
creator: Ava Kim
description: Implement a runtime-level enforcement layer that ensures requests from customers who require EU-only processing are pinned to EU regions and EU-resident model variants. This ticket defines the allowlist/denylist model for customers, residency tagging for models and deployments, the policy evaluation path in the router, and pragmatic rollback/fallback behavior to preserve availability while maintaining compliance guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can evaluate per-request customer residency constraint and route to EU region endpoints when 'eu_only' is set
Customer-level allowlist and denylist can be configured via Console and respected by the runtime router within 100ms decision latency
Model deployments are annotated with residency tags (eu, global, regional) and router will avoid routing to non-eu-tagged model variants for eu_only customers

Fallback rules exist: if EU capacity is exhausted, either queue with backpressure, surface a deterministic 409 + user-facing guidance, or route to pre-approved EU fallback variant; no silent routing to non-EU endpoints
Audit log entries contain customer id, evaluated policy, chosen route, and model variant id for every routed request for at least 90 days
E2E tests cover allowlist/denylist permutations, residency-tag mismatches, and fallback paths with mock capacity exhaustion
Feature gated behind an admin Console toggle and rollout to a pilot customer group before general availability
tasks: Design policy schema for customer residency constraints and allowlist/denylist (PM & Security)
Add residency tags to model catalog and deployment metadata in Control Plane
Extend router policy evaluator to include residency tag checks and allowlist/denylist lookup
Implement fast in-memory cache for tenant policy with invalidation path from control plane
Console UI: tenant settings page to mark 'EU-only' and configure allowlist/denylist and fallback preference
Add audit logging hook and retention pipeline for routing decisions
E2E integration tests and load tests to validate decision latency under 99th percentile
Run pilot with 2 customers and iterate on rollout docs and runbooks
comments: 2026-02-22 Ava Kim: Kickoff done with PM and Security. Agreed on three fallback modes (hold, fail-fast, EU-fallback-variant). Security flagged audit retention requirement.

2026-02-27 Priya Nair (PM): Updated requirements - prefer deterministic 409 + user guidance when EU capacity is exceeded for regulated customers; allow explicit per-customer override to use global variants with contractual opt-in.
2026-03-03 Diego Alvarez: Prototype of in-memory tenant policy cache merged to feature branch. Decision latency measured at ~12ms for policy lookup in synthetic benchmark.
2026-03-06 Security Review (notes): Need KMS audit for whether sensitive metadata is logged; confirm PII redaction in audit entries. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-09 Design feedback (Maya Patel): Console UX flows should provide a readable compliance summary and a 'simulate' button to test routing for sample requests. Added to tasks.

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez: Began implementing residency tag propagation for model deployments. Open question: how to represent multi-region deployments (eu + na) - proposal to add granularity 'primary_region' + 'expanded_regions'.
implementation_notes: The router will evaluate in this order: tenant static constraint -> per-request override header (only for enterprise tokens and logged) -> capacity availability -> fallback policy. Use token-scoped metadata for fast path. Cache TTL should be short (30s) but support immediate invalidation on Console change. Ensure the path is idempotent and metrics tagged with 'eu_policy_evaluated' and 'eu_policy_decision'.
rollout_plan: Feature will be behind feature flag 'eu_sov_routing_v1'. Stage 1: internal dogfood. Stage 2: pilot with two EU-regulated customers (legal sign-off required). Stage 3: soft launch to all EU-marked customers with monitoring thresholds. Stage 4: GA after 4 weeks of pilot with no major incidents.
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator and residency tag parser
Integration tests with control plane metadata updates and router invalidation
Chaos test to simulate EU region capacity exhaustion and validate deterministic fallback behavior
Audit log verification to ensure no PII and 90-day retention works end-to-end
